questions.text: Classify Signals: Continuous-Time vs Discrete-Time, Periodic vs Aperiodic ($x(t+T) = x(t)$), Energy vs Power signals ($E = \int_{-\infty}^\infty |x(t)|^2 dt, P = \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{T}\int_{-T/2}^{T/2} |x(t)|^2 dt$), Even vs Odd signals ($x_e(t) = \frac{x(t)+x(-t)}{2}, x_o(t) = \frac{x(t)-x(-t)}{2}$), and Deterministic vs Random signals.

Define elementary signals: Unit Step $u(t)$, Dirac Delta Function $\delta(t)$ (and its sifting property $\int_{-\infty}^\infty x(t)\delta(t-t_0)dt = x(t_0)$), Unit Ramp $r(t)$, and Complex Exponential. Perform transformations: Time Shifting, Time Reversal, and Time Scaling on a given waveform $x(t)$ to plot $y(t) = x(2t - 3)$ and $z(t) = x(-t/2 + 1)$.

Define System Properties: (a) Linearity (Superposition and Homogeneity), (b) Time-Invariance, (c) Causality, (d) Stability (BIBO Stability $\int |h(t)|dt < \infty$), (e) Memory / Static, and (f) Invertibility. Test whether $y(t) = t^2 x(t) + 3$ and $y[n] = x[2n]$ are linear, time-invariant, and causal.

Explain Convolution Integral ($y(t) = x(t) * h(t) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty x(\tau)h(t-\tau)d\tau$) and Discrete Convolution Sum ($y[n] = \sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty x[k]h[n-k]$). Convolve two rectangular pulses $x(t) = u(t) - u(t-2)$ and $h(t) = u(t) - u(t-3)$ analytically and sketch the resulting trapezoidal output waveform.

State Dirichlet's Conditions for Fourier Series convergence. Derive Exponential Fourier Series ($x(t) = \sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty c_k e^{jk\omega_0 t}$) and Trigonometric Fourier Series. Calculate the Fourier coefficients for a symmetric square wave and full-wave rectified sine wave.

Define Continuous-Time Fourier Transform (CTFT) ($X(j\omega) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty x(t)e^{-j\omega t}dt$) and Inverse CTFT. State and prove CTFT Properties: Linearity, Time Shifting ($x(t-t_0) \leftrightarrow e^{-j\omega t_0}X(j\omega)$), Frequency Shifting (Modulation), Time Scaling, Differentiation in Time, Convolution Property ($x(t)*h(t) \leftrightarrow X(j\omega)H(j\omega)$), and Parseval's Energy Theorem.

State the Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem. Explain Aliasing effect and anti-aliasing filter. Find the minimum Nyquist Rate and Nyquist Interval for the signal $x(t) = 10\cos(400\pi t)\text{sinc}(200\pi t)$.

Define Bilateral (Two-Sided) and Unilateral (One-Sided) Laplace Transform ($X(s) = \int_{0^-}^\infty x(t)e^{-st}dt$). Explain the Region of Convergence (ROC) properties on the s-plane. Find the Laplace transform and ROC of: (a) $x(t) = e^{-at}u(t)$, and (b) $x(t) = -e^{-at}u(-t)$.

Solve the second-order LTI differential equation using Laplace Transform with initial conditions: $\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} + 5\frac{dy}{dt} + 6y(t) = 2x(t)$ with $y(0^-) = 1, y'(0^-) = 0$, and input $x(t) = u(t)$. Find Zero-Input Response (ZIR), Zero-State Response (ZSR), and Total Response.

Define Z-Transform ($X(z) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^\infty x[n] z^{-n}$) and Region of Convergence (ROC) on the z-plane. State ROC properties for finite, right-sided, left-sided, and two-sided sequences. Determine the Z-transform and ROC of $x[n] = a^n u[n] - b^n u[-n-1]$.

Explain Inverse Z-Transform methods: Partial Fraction Expansion, Power Series (Long Division), and Contour Integration (Residue method). Find $x[n]$ for $X(z) = \frac{1 - \frac{1}{2}z^{-1}}{(1 - \frac{1}{4}z^{-1})(1 - \frac{1}{3}z^{-1})}$ for causal ROC $|z| > 1/3$.
Solve the discrete-time difference equation using Z-Transform: $y[n] - 0.5y[n-1] = x[n]$ with initial condition $y[-1] = 2$ and input $x[n] = (0.25)^n u[n]$.
